contracts.commit_point: The spawn of the bash child process: subprocess.Popen(self.cmd, ...) inside PTYSession.__init__ (src/Tools/session.py:60-68), reached from run_session via _create_session (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:279) and from run_session_async via asyncio.shield(self._create_session_async(...)) (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:311), each after Session.__init__ constructs and starts the PTYSession (src/Tools/session.py:234-235). Guard rejection occurs earlier in the same entry point, before cmd_full = ['bash','-lc',cmd] is built (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:276 and 308).
contracts.declared_mechanism: check_cmd (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:18-43) imports COMMAND_EXECUTION_VALIDATION_RULES (src/config.py:36), a creator-keyed registry of CmdFilterList entries where 'ctf_agent' maps to BlackOrWhite.BLACK with cmd_list=['bash'] (src/config.py:28-33); it splits the command with shlex, extracts the head token, and returns False when the head token is in a BLACK rule's cmd_list. run_session (line 270) and run_session_async (line 302) invoke check_cmd first and return a rejection message ('The command ... is not allowed to be executed.') — or a validation-failure message on exception (lines 272-274, 304-306) — before constructing cmd_full and creating the session.
contracts.forbidden_condition: check_cmd(cmd, creater) evaluates to False — i.e., the command's head token matches an entry of a BLACK-type CmdFilterList in COMMAND_EXECUTION_VALIDATION_RULES (e.g., 'bash' in the 'ctf_agent' rule) — while the run_session/run_session_async path nonetheless proceeds past validation to build ['bash','-lc',cmd] and create a Session.
pending_binding_information: check_cmd's rule-selection loop reuses the identifier 'creater' as the loop variable, shadowing the function parameter, so the source-literal creator-scoping comparison at src/Tools/SessionManager.py:34-36 does not clearly express the intended per-creator rule lookup; whether the 'ctf_agent' rule is selected only for that creator requires confirmation beyond the supplied text.

Agent-side binding is unresolved: no supplied source view shows a tool registration, decorator, dispatch table, or lifecycle hook that invokes run_session/run_session_async with an agent-controlled cmd/creater; identifying such wiring (if any) is required to upgrade agent_mediation from not_established.

The provenance of the 'creater' argument (e.g., whether it is an agent identifier such as 'ctf_agent' supplied by agent code) and of the 'cmd' string (whether agent-generated) is not shown in the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of a caller-supplied command string through SessionManager.run_session (sync, src/Tools/SessionManager.py:259) or SessionManager.run_session_async (async, src/Tools/SessionManager.py:290), each of which validates via check_cmd, packages the command as ['bash','-lc',cmd], and creates a PTY-backed Session from the manager workspace.
contracts.protected_resource: The PTY-backed bash child process (PTYSession.proc spawned by subprocess.Popen in src/Tools/session.py:60-68) executing 'bash -lc <cmd>' with cwd set to the session manager workspace (SESSION_MANAGER_WORKSPACE_DIR), together with its pseudo-terminal (pty.openpty, src/Tools/session.py:56).
contracts.protection_obligation: Commands whose head token (first token of shlex.split) appears in the creator-keyed blacklist registered in COMMAND_EXECUTION_VALIDATION_RULES (e.g., head token 'bash' for 'ctf_agent') must be rejected by check_cmd inside SessionManager.run_session and SessionManager.run_session_async before a session is created and the 'bash -lc <cmd>' PTY subprocess is spawned.
scope_limits: Applies only to the head token produced by shlex.split(cmd) (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:32-33); non-head tokens, arguments, and sub-commands reached via shell metacharacters are not part of the matched condition.

Default-allow semantics: an empty rule set (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:30-31) or a head token matching no rule (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:42-43) permits execution; only explicit BLACK-rule head-token hits are rejected.

Covers only the session-creation entry points run_session/run_session_async; input_session/input_session_async writes into already-running sessions (src/Tools/SessionManager.py:359-419) and direct Session/PTYSession construction are not routed through check_cmd in the supplied source.
The rule set is the import-time static content of COMMAND_EXECUTION_VALIDATION_RULES (src/config.py:36); dynamic configuration changes are outside this contract.
This contract records the declared source-supported obligation only; it does not assert DEC violation, safety, runtime effectiveness, or prevalence.

missing_information: No supplied source view contains agent-side wiring (tool registry, decorator, dispatch table, or agent lifecycle hook) connecting agent turns to SessionManager.run_session/run_session_async; agent mediation of the command-execution effect therefore cannot be bound from the supplied source, and the config.py/module-docstring mentions of 'LLM'/'Agent' are treated as topic metadata, not binding evidence.

Provenance of the 'creater' argument (e.g., whether it equals an agent identifier such as 'ctf_agent' supplied by agent code) and of the 'cmd' string (whether agent-generated input) is not shown in the supplied views.
Alternative or direct construction paths for Session/PTYSession that would bypass check_cmd are not enumerated in the supplied views.

Runtime behavior, safety, and prevalence labels are unavailable per the stated scope; the effective creator-scoping semantics of check_cmd given the loop-variable shadowing at src/Tools/SessionManager.py:34-36 cannot be settled from the literal source text alone.
